candidate_snapshot.subject: business_studies
candidate_snapshot.body: A firm has a stronger cash-flow position and is comparing debt financing with equity financing. Which inference is supported by the stated financing factor?

options.text: The firm should declare a dividend before assessing finance.
Equity must always be chosen because it has no repayment date.
Strong cash flow rules out borrowing.
Debt financing may be more viable than equity financing.

candidate_snapshot.explanation: The source states that a stronger cash-flow position may make debt financing more viable than funding through equity. It does not make debt compulsory.

learning_objective.objective: Apply the relevant financial management or financial planning principle to the printed question.

actual_explanation_claim_review.exact_quote: The source states that a stronger cash-flow position may make debt financing more viable than funding through equity
It does not make debt compulsory.
actual_explanation_claim_review.assessment: Supported modal inference: possibility is not compulsion.

decisive_source.exact_full_text:
(d) Cash Flow Position of the Company:
A stronger cash flow position may
make debt financing more viable
than funding through equity.
(e) Fixed Operating Costs: If a business
has high fixed operating costs (e.g.,
building rent, Insurance premium,
Salaries, etc.), It must reduce fixed
financing costs. Hence, lower debt
financing is better. Similarly, if
fixed operating cost is less, more
of debt financing may be preferred.

syllabus.exact_quote: Financial decisions: investing, financing and dividend-Meaning and factors affecting.
syllabus.assessment: Explicit financing decisions and factors entitlement; capital structure factors also printed.

option_review.A: Dividend-first step unsupported by stated factor; not a rival answer.
option_review.B: Always-equity necessity unsupported; partial truth of repayment-date clause cannot validate full conclusion.
option_review.C: Borrowing prohibition conflicts with debt-may-be-more-viable inference.
option_review.D: Faithful qualified source inference; unique answer.

blind_reports_summary.derivation: The supplied NCERT excerpt says a stronger cash-flow position may make debt financing more viable than equity. That supports D as a possibility, not a mandatory choice. The excerpt does not support declaring a dividend first, always choosing equity, or ruling out borrowing.

Under financing decisions (and capital structure determinants), a stronger cash flow position provides the liquidity needed to service interest and principal repayments, making debt financing more viable than equity financing.

issues.detail: D closely echoes the source, while A–C are broad or readily excluded; closer, plausible distractors could improve discrimination.
